message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 16 November 2026 23:40 to 17 November 2026 23:40 UTC (17 November 05:10 to 18 November 05:10 IST).
**Scope:** Products.txt and List_of_SIA_Completed.txt, combined and deduplicated, plus the mandatory MongoDB ecosystem sweep.

New relevant Java vulnerabilities were reported in this window. Installed versions and exposure must be checked to determine actual impact.

### OpenJDK and Oracle Java: CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell)
**Severity:** High, CVSS 3.1 8.1 according to Oracle; the discovering researchers report Critical, CVSS 4.0 9.2. These use different scoring versions.
**Issue:** A Base64 decoder memory-corruption flaw can permit memory disclosure or code execution under particular runtime, processor and application conditions. Researchers demonstrated exploitation in applications including Jenkins, Keycloak and Elasticsearch.
**Relevance:** OpenJDK, Oracle Java, Jenkins, Keycloak and Elasticsearch are in the primary lists; affected runtime and hardware conditions still need verification. Oracle lists affected supported Java SE versions in its advisory. [Oracle advisory](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html#AppendixJAVA); [researcher disclosure](https://calif.io/java4shell/).

### Oracle Java SE: additional November security fixes
**Severity:** Up to High, CVSS 3.1 7.5 for the additional issues; scores vary by CVE.
**Issue:** Oracle's 17 November security update includes 11 Java SE patches in total, including CVE-2026-114938 above. The remaining issues affect components including JavaFX, authentication, TLS, libraries and HotSpot; Oracle says they may be remotely exploitable without authentication, subject to the conditions in its risk matrix.
**Relevance:** Oracle Java is on the monitored list. The affected supported versions vary by CVE; consult the [Oracle Java SE risk matrix](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cspunov2026.html#AppendixJAVA) against installed versions. The additional fixes are grouped here and do not duplicate the Java4Shell finding.

### MongoDB ecosystem
No new relevant MongoDB vulnerability was verified in the window. The sweep covered Server and editions, mongod/mongos, Atlas, management services, Compass, mongosh, tools, Kubernetes operators, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, integrations and MongoDB-owned advisories across vendor, CVE, GitHub, CISA and research searches. MongoDB's [CVE-2026-118383 notice](https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/important-mongodb-security-update-available-action-required-november-10-2026/344843) is dated 10 November and is outside this window.

**Closing:** Prompt review of Java deployments is recommended given the reported severity and potential impact. Search coverage across the extensive inventory is necessarily limited; no finding is not proof of absence. Entries such as “F”, “PMP”, “SIP” and “Carbon” were too ambiguous to match confidently and were not treated as precise product identities.
